subject: art-design
topicDisplay: Component 2: Investigating the Creative and Cultural Industries
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a creative and cultural industry?
questions.explain: Fashion and textiles design is a recognised creative and cultural industry, whereas the others are primary or heavy industries.

questions.q: Which cultural institution exists to display artwork to the public?
questions.explain: Museums and galleries are cultural institutions that exhibit artworks for public access.

questions.q: The term 'creative industries' broadly refers to sectors that generate value from what?
questions.explain: Creative industries are defined by their basis in individual creativity, skill and talent.

questions.q: A student wants a career designing packaging, posters and advertising layouts. Which sector suits them best?
questions.explain: Graphic design covers visual communication for products, packaging and advertising.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a gallery within the cultural industries?
options: To collect, preserve and exhibit artworks for public access
questions.explain: Galleries collect, conserve and display art so the public can view and engage with it.

questions.q: Which of these is a craft-based creative industry?
questions.explain: Ceramics and pottery is a craft discipline within the creative industries.

questions.q: A professional who designs buildings and structures is called a(n):
questions.explain: An architect designs buildings and the built environment.

questions.q: Who creates images to accompany text in books and magazines?
questions.explain: An illustrator produces images that support or accompany written text.

questions.q: What is the role of a curator in a gallery?
options: To select, organise and interpret artworks for exhibition
To paint murals on the walls
questions.explain: A curator chooses, arranges and interprets works to shape an exhibition.

questions.q: A textile designer primarily works with:
questions.explain: Textile designers create patterns and surface designs for fabrics and materials.

questions.q: A studio needs someone to create moving images and characters for an animated film. Which role should they hire?
questions.explain: An animator creates the moving images and characters used in animation.

questions.q: What is a graphic designer's main responsibility?
options: To communicate messages visually through typography, image and layout
questions.explain: Graphic designers combine type, image and layout to communicate messages visually.

questions.q: A client wants a unique handmade ring designed and crafted from silver. Which specialist is most appropriate?
questions.explain: A jewellery designer or silversmith designs and makes items such as rings from precious metals.

questions.q: A photographer working in the creative industries primarily uses:
questions.explain: Photographers use cameras to capture and produce images.

questions.q: Contextual research in Art and Design involves studying:
options: The work of other artists, designers, cultures and movements
questions.explain: Contextual research examines the work of others and the cultural context around it.

questions.q: Which of the following is a primary source for contextual research?
options: Visiting a gallery and observing an artwork first-hand
A reproduction printed in a textbook
A summary found on a website
questions.explain: A primary source is first-hand material, such as directly viewing the actual artwork.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a secondary source?
options: Information from others' accounts such as books, websites and reproductions
Direct observation of the real artwork
Your own drawing made from life
A live model posing in front of you
questions.explain: Secondary sources are second-hand, such as reproductions, books and websites.

questions.q: To gather primary-source research on a sculptor's work, what is the best action?
options: Visit an exhibition and draw or photograph the sculptures in person
Copy a picture from a website
Ask a friend to describe them
questions.explain: First-hand observation of the actual works provides primary-source research.

questions.q: Why is contextual research important when developing your own artwork?
options: It helps generate ideas and inform creative decisions
It replaces the need to make any artwork
It is only useful to historians
questions.explain: Studying context inspires ideas and informs how you develop your own work.

questions.q: In contextual research, an art movement such as Impressionism or Cubism is best described as:
options: A group of artists sharing a common style or approach in a period
questions.explain: An art movement is a shared style or approach adopted by a group of artists in a period.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Art and Design (2017) specification; Component 2: Investigating the Creative and Cultural Industries
